findings.reason: the branch selects between "seven documents delivered" and "no documents, source back to the lead", so an undefined predicate lets a worker close on the wrong one and the blocked plan inherits the result, not the deliveries.
findings.text: §5 closes in one of two ways, but the two branches share one observation: the success branch permits "each of the seven listed documents is fetched at its stated version, or reported with its outcome (not found, not permitted, a sign-in page, an error) where the host refuses it", while the failure branch fires when "the first named document cannot be fetched", so a first document the host refuses (404, 403, or a sign-in page) satisfies both forms, and nothing fixes which of the seven is probed or in what order, letting the worker choose which branch — and therefore whether the document source stays with the section or goes back to the lead — on evidence the plan does not discriminate

— §5 states "That host is read under the same rules as the two records hosts" and requires "Tests show every write-refusal and host-refusal case of section 2 holds for the document host", yet §2's delivered rule (plan.html:46) says "Requests go only to the ICP hosts listed in private configuration ... the integration instance ... and the production instance" and its host-refusal test (plan.html:47) refuses "any host other than the ICP hosts listed in private configuration and the listed sign-in hosts"; the IDM document host is neither an ICP host nor a sign-in host, so §2's rule refuses the host §5 is built on, and a worker applying §2's test literally must make the section's own first fetch. WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — REASON: the same shape of conflict was resolved for production by naming it in §2; the document host needs the same allowance stated in §2's delivered host set (with the named-identity restriction), or §5's tests and the section's fetch contradict the guardrails they are meant to inherit.

— the plan declares `plan-blocks` = `iter-signal-context-and-enrichment`, whose §4 (`docs/plans/iter-signal-context-and-enrichment.html:58`) now depends on `icp-api-access#s3`, `#s4` and `#s5` and delivers "the rows of its signal list and data file, and references to its functional specification", while §5's failure branch (plan.html:61) closes the section as done with "nothing further is requested from the host", no document fetched, and the document source going back to the lead — so the dependency the relationship names can be satisfied while delivering none of the files the blocked section imports; the block is claimed against a section whose done-when permits delivering nothing. WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — REASON: a blocks relationship that a no-fetch close satisfies will release that plan's §4 to build pilot context with no signal list or specification, which is the empty delivery the earlier wiring finding named; either the relationship must record that only §5's fetch branch unblocks it, or the blocked plan's done-when must fail on missing documents.
